items.title: ‘She’s living the dream’: My stepmother said I can buy my childhood home for $850,000. Is she taking advantage of me?
items.content: “My late father bought our house for $250,000 in the 1990s.”

items.title: My spouse was awarded $90,000 from my 401(k) in our divorce. How is that fair?
items.content: “I retired in 2020 and subsequently went through a divorce a few years later.”

items.title: ‘I don’t feel sorry for myself’: I’m 64 and will be renting for the rest of my life. Is that so bad?
items.content: “I married a wonderful man with a good income. He left his job due to health issues and suffered a massive stroke at 53.”

items.title: Will Anthropic pull off a November IPO? Time is running out to file key paperwork.
items.content: If market pressures keep building, Anthropic “could reasonably decide it is better to stay private and wait for a better opportunity,” one portfolio manager says.

items.title: Investors piled a record sum into a leveraged semiconductor ETF last week. Things didn’t work out.
items.content: Traders making bullish bets on chip stocks are getting walloped this month, as renewed fears emerged about investment returns on the buildout of artificial intelligence.

items.title: This hot AI-fueled stock has been in a rut. It just beat earnings expectations by 36%.
items.content: A company beating earnings expectations by 36% and revenue expectations by 15% would usually see a postresults bump. But not for Bloom Energy, the fuel-cell maker that has flourished due to data-center demand.

items.title: The mobile ambitions of SpaceX are hitting telecom stocks again. Here’s what the latest developments mean.
items.content: Reports of Starlink’s discussions with cell-tower owners were noticed by shareholders of Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile.

items.title: The real test for Moderna’s cancer vaccine isn’t about beating Keytruda. It’s keeping cancer from coming back in the long term.
items.content: The first Phase 3 data for a cancer vaccine has raised questions about whether the potential new treatment is needed.

items.title: Some Republicans are opposing Trump on tariffs. Maine’s Susan Collins just got him to back down on Canadian levies.
items.content: As she faces a tough midterm race, the five-term GOP senator is touting her successful lobbying effort against certain tariffs on Canada

items.title: The U.S. economy is great by this measure, and the good times aren’t over. So why are Americans so sour?
items.content: A once-in-a-generation investment boom has created lots of winners — but many Americans are feeling left out.
